extra.message: User-controlled `name` parameter is interpolated into SQL query using Python `%` string formatting ('%(name)s') instead of parameterized query placeholders. The resulting string is passed directly to cursor.execute() with no binding. An attacker can inject arbitrary SQL via the student name field on POST /students/. Contrast with Review.create() and Course.create() which correctly use parameterized queries.

Jinja2 autoescaping is explicitly set to False (autoescape=False). This disables automatic HTML escaping of all template variables, making every user-controlled value rendered in templates vulnerable to Cross-Site Scripting (XSS). This is the root enabler for multiple stored XSS vulnerabilities in this application.

User-submitted review text (from POST /courses/{id}/review) is rendered as {{ review.review_text }} without any escaping. Since autoescape is disabled, an attacker can inject arbitrary HTML/JavaScript via the review form, which is stored in the database and executed in every visitor's browser who views the course page. This is a stored XSS vulnerability.

Course title (user-submitted via POST /courses/) is rendered as {{ course.title }} without escaping. Since autoescape is disabled, an attacker with admin access (or via CSRF since CSRF protection is disabled) can inject HTML/JavaScript in the course title, which is stored and executed for all visitors viewing the course page.

Course description (user-submitted via POST /courses/) is rendered as {{ course.description }} without escaping. Since autoescape is disabled, an attacker can inject HTML/JavaScript in the course description field, resulting in stored XSS.
Course title rendered as {{ course.title }} without escaping in the courses listing page. Stored XSS via the course creation form.
Course description rendered as {{ course.description }} without escaping in the courses listing page. Stored XSS via the course creation form.

Student name rendered as {{ name }} without escaping in the students listing page. Since autoescape is disabled and Student.create() is also vulnerable to SQL injection, an attacker can inject HTML/JavaScript via the student name field. Note that student.jinja2 uses the `| e` filter but students.jinja2 does not.
Course title rendered as {{ course.title }} without escaping in the review page template. Stored XSS via the course creation form propagates to the review page.
Student name rendered as {{ student.name }} without escaping in the evaluate error template. Stored XSS via the student name field propagates to the evaluation error page.

CSRF middleware is commented out (# csrf_middleware), leaving all POST endpoints unprotected against Cross-Site Request Forgery. An attacker can trick authenticated users into submitting forms that create students, courses, reviews, or evaluate marks. The templates even include _csrf_token hidden fields, but the server never validates them.

POST /students/ creates a new student without any authentication check. The `students` view handler has no @authorize() decorator and no manual auth check before processing the POST request. Any unauthenticated user can create students.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: POST /courses/{id}/review creates a review without any authentication check. The `review` view handler has no @authorize() decorator and no manual auth check before processing the POST request. Any unauthenticated user can submit reviews.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: POST /courses/ creates a course without checking that the user is an admin. While the template (courses.jinja2:25) restricts the form to admin users, the view handler performs no authorization check. Any authenticated or unauthenticated user can create courses via a direct POST request.

POST /students/{id}/evaluate/{id} creates a mark/grade without checking that the user is an admin. The course.jinja2 template (line 41) restricts the evaluate form to admin users only, but the `evaluate` view handler performs no authorization check. Any unauthenticated user can assign grades to students.

Password verification uses unsalted MD5 hash comparison: `self.pwd_hash == md5(password.encode('utf-8')).hexdigest()`. MD5 is cryptographically broken and unsuitable for password hashing. No salt is used, making all password hashes vulnerable to rainbow table attacks. Should use a dedicated password hashing function like bcrypt, scrypt, or argon2.

cwe: CWE-916: Use of Password Hash With Insufficient Computational Effort

extra.message: Database credentials are hardcoded in the configuration file: user 'postgres' with password 'postgres'. This file is tracked in version control, exposing credentials to anyone with repository access.

Session cookie is created with httponly=False in RedisStorage, making the session cookie accessible to JavaScript. Combined with the XSS vulnerabilities present in this application, an attacker can steal session cookies via injected scripts.
The aiohttp Application is instantiated with debug=True. Debug mode can expose sensitive information including stack traces, application internals, and configuration details in error responses.

The 50x error template renders {{ error.__dict__ }} which dumps the entire exception object's internal state, potentially exposing stack traces, internal paths, database query details, and other sensitive information to end users.

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information
